physical_harm: The deceased suffered multiple incised and penetrating wounds, leading to excessive haemorrhage and death due to injuries to the right lung and liver.
number_of_offences: 3 offences were charged, 1 was finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The evidence of PW-6, an independent witness, was accepted as crucial as it completely ruled out the presence of PW-5 at the scene of the offence and cast doubt on the presence of PWs 13 and 14.
witness_credibility: The court assessed PW-5 as a highly interested and partisan witness whose evidence was required to be carefully scrutinised. The court also found that PW-6's evidence was unimpeached and binding on the prosecution.

legal_representation.accused: A. Sharan, AK. Singh, Samir Ali Khan

investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, investigation kept pending under Section 173(8) Cr.P.C.

appeal_history.high_court: Set aside conviction under Sections 148 and 201, upheld conviction under Section 302 IPC
appeal_history.supreme_court: Allowed the appeal, set aside conviction and directed release

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused persons equipped with deadly weapons reached the scene of occurrence and inflicted injuries on the deceased and others, leading to the deceased's death. The case was based on the Parcha Bayan lodged by PW-5, and the trial court accepted the prosecution's case.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the incident took place out of acute enmity and that the evidence of highly interested eye-witnesses should be rejected as there is a likelihood of implicating innocent persons. The defence also highlighted the presence of independent witnesses whose evidence contradicted the prosecution's case.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that concurrent findings of facts are not usually interfered with by the court under Article 136 of the Constitution of India unless it is clearly established that the courts below altogether ignored vital piece of evidence and rested their conclusion on evidence that cannot be accepted on the face of it.
precedent_relied_upon: Mukhtiar Ahmed Ansari v. State (NCT of Delhi) (2005) 5 sec 258
